data.title: Lymphogranuloma venereum — viva
data.summary: Sexually transmitted infections · 15 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Lymphogranuloma venereum** (Sexually transmitted infections)_

**Q1. What is LGV? Agent?**
- Systemic STI of lymphatic tissue caused by invasive Chlamydia trachomatis serovars L1, L2 (commonest; L2b in MSM proctitis outbreaks), L3
- Obligate intracellular; elementary body (infectious) and reticulate body (replicative)

**Q2. Describe the three stages.**
- Primary (3–30 days): small painless papule, herpetiform ulcer or urethritis/cervicitis — transient, often unnoticed
- Secondary (2–6 weeks later): inguinal syndrome — painful, usually unilateral inguinal/femoral lymphadenitis, matted, may suppurate with multiple sinuses (unlike single opening in chancroid); fever, malaise, arthralgia, erythema nodosum/multiforme; anorectal syndrome in receptive anal sex/women — haemorrhagic proctocolitis
- Tertiary (late): genitoanorectal syndrome — chronic lymphatic obstruction and fibrosis: esthiomene, elephantiasis of genitals, rectal stricture, fistulae, perianal lymphorrhoids, frozen pelvis

**Q3. What is the groove sign?**
- Enlarged inguinal nodes above and femoral nodes below the inguinal (Poupart's) ligament separated by a groove — seen in ~20%; suggestive but not diagnostic

**Q4. What is esthiomene? (PYQ)**
- Chronic progressive hypertrophy and ulceration ('eating away') of the vulva due to lymphatic obstruction from LGV — elephantiasis with ulcers, fistulae; also seen with donovanosis, TB, filariasis
- Management: long antibiotic course + reconstructive surgery (vulvectomy/plastic)

**Q5. What is the Frei test?**
- Historical intradermal skin test with LGV antigen (delayed hypersensitivity) — obsolete because of poor specificity and safety

**Q6. Investigations.**
- NAAT (PCR) of ulcer swab, bubo aspirate or rectal swab for C. trachomatis with genotyping for L serovars (best)
- Serology: complement fixation titre ≥1:64 or microimmunofluorescence ≥1:256 supports LGV
- Culture in McCoy cells (rarely done); Giemsa — Gamna–Favre inclusion bodies
- Exclude syphilis, HIV, chancroid

**Q7. Differential diagnosis of inguinal bubo.**
- Chancroid (painful single opening), syphilis (painless rubbery), donovanosis pseudobubo, herpes (tender small nodes), TB lymphadenitis, plague, cat-scratch disease, lymphoma/metastatic nodes, filariasis, pyogenic lymphadenitis from leg infection, incarcerated hernia

**Q8. Treatment.**
- Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 21 days (drug of choice)
- Alternatives: erythromycin 500 mg four times daily for 21 days (pregnancy), azithromycin 1 g weekly for 3 weeks
- NACO black kit (doxycycline 21 days + azithromycin 1 g) for bubo
- Aspirate fluctuant nodes through healthy skin; do not incise (sinus formation); surgery for late strictures/elephantiasis
- Treat contacts in last 60 days

**Q9. Differentiate LGV proctitis from inflammatory bowel disease.**
- LGV: MSM/receptive anal sex, rapid onset, rectal pain, tenesmus, mucopurulent bloody discharge, PCR positive, rapid response to doxycycline
- Crohn's: chronic, skip lesions, perianal fistula, granulomas, no infection
- Histology can look similar — always test rectal swab

**Q10. Complications?**
- Rectal stricture, rectovaginal fistula, lymphoedema/elephantiasis of genitals ('saxophone penis'), esthiomene, infertility, rarely SCC; systemic — hepatitis, pneumonitis, meningitis

**Q11. Describe the pathogenesis of LGV.**
- L serovars infect macrophages and travel through lymphatics → lymphadenitis with stellate abscesses (necrosis with surrounding palisading histiocytes) → suppuration, sinus formation, chronic lymphatic obstruction and fibrosis → elephantiasis and strictures

**Q12. Histopathology of LGV lymph node.**
- Stellate (star-shaped) abscesses with central neutrophils and necrosis surrounded by palisaded epithelioid histiocytes — also seen in cat-scratch disease, tularaemia, Yersinia, fungal infections

**Q13. What is 'saxophone penis'?**
- Late LGV lymphoedema of the penis and scrotum producing a deformed, swollen, twisted penis — also from filariasis or chronic HS; needs reconstructive surgery

**Q14. LGV in MSM — current epidemiology.**
- Outbreaks of L2b proctitis among men who have sex with men (Europe, North America) often with HIV co-infection; may be asymptomatic rectal carriage; test rectal swabs with NAAT and genotype

**Q15. What is the follow-up and partner management?**
- Clinical follow-up until resolution (bubo/ proctitis); test-of-cure NAAT for rectal infection after 3–4 weeks in some guidelines; treat all partners within 60 days with doxycycline 7 days (or full LGV course if symptomatic); screen for HIV, syphilis, hepatitis

## Quick spotter facts
- Groove sign — LGV
- Esthiomene — chronic ulcerating vulval elephantiasis
- Doxycycline 21 days (black kit)

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (LGV); NACO National Technical Guidelines on RTI/STI (syndromic management, colour-coded kits). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
